Household size (2018–23 pace): household size continues linearly from 2023 at the 2018–2023 census-
   interval pace instead of the Stats NZ household-size path rebased on 2023.
Population (5th–95th pct.): Stats NZ 2024-base stochastic projection, 5th / 95th percentile path instead
   of the median.
Household size (smaller–larger households): Stats NZ Low / High household-size variant (smaller / larger
   households) instead of the Medium variant.
Household size after 2043: end-slope taper: from the shape-preserving (PCHIP) end slope at 2043 the
   slope tapers to zero over 5 years, instead of a zero slope imposed at 2043 and household size held
   constant after 2043.
Household size after 2043: secant-slope taper: the last published interval (2038–2043) linear at its
   secant slope, the slope then tapering to zero over 5 years, instead of a zero slope imposed at 2043
   and household size held constant after 2043.
2026 overbuild booked as stock-neutral redevelopment: the 2026 overbuild (building above need in
   2026–2027 and its continuation, fading at ρ = 0.43) replaces existing dwellings instead of adding to
   the stock: no surplus, so no absorption payback and no soil carbon loss on it.
Dwelling-size reference window 2016–2025: new-dwelling size held at its 2016–2025 mean per typology
   instead of the 2023–2025 mean.
Completion rate (0.93–0.96): 0.93 / 0.96 of consented dwellings completed instead of 0.945.
Vacancy rate: 1986–2023 census mean: the mean of the 1986–2023 censuses on one definition instead of the
   2023 census value (5.39%).
Overbuild absorbed (by 2030–by 2045): the 2026 overbuild absorbed by 2030 / 2045 instead of 2035.
Completion lag (15–19 months): consents lagged 15 / 19 months instead of 17.

NZ-made electricity-intensive
items held at 2025 factors

No 2026 data (consents to Dec 2025): consents to December 2025 and the projected 2026 population instead
   of consents to July 2026 and the observed 2026 population growth.
Replacement (Low–Very High): Low: the 1991–2023 long-run net rate throughout; High (tick): the 2018–2023
   rate persists; Very High: the 1991–2023 census-interval trend continues; instead of the 2018–2023
   rate fading to the long-run rate with a 10-year half-life.
Replacement half-life (5–15 yr): 5 / 15 years instead of 10.
Soil order (Raw–Organic): the soil carbon loss of the lowest (Raw) / highest (Organic) soil order on
   every new footprint instead of the area-weighted mean over the soil orders of the Auckland land zoned
   for urbanisation.
Single case study (lowest–highest): the materials factor of the lowest / highest single case study of
   each typology instead of the pooled typology factor.
Frozen technology (2025 factors held): every factor held at 2025 instead of A1–A3 on the item paths of
   Horup et al. (2025) and A4–A5 falling 1% per year.
Carbon factors (jackknife): the lowest / highest pooled materials factor when each case study is left
   out in turn, instead of the pooled factor (a spread, not a confidence interval).
NZ-made electricity-intensive items held at 2025 factors: items made in New Zealand with electricity-
   intensive production held at 2025 instead of following their Horup et al. (2025) path.
A4–A5 decarbonisation (own path–held at 2025): A4–A5 on each item's own Horup et al. (2025) path / held
   at 2025 instead of the generic 1% per year decline (Resch et al. 2021).
Soil carbon loss on all floor area, incl. replacement: soil carbon loss also on replacement floor area
   instead of none on rebuilt footprints.
Proxy-mapped items held at 2025 factors: items mapped to a proxy material held at 2025 instead of
   following the proxy's path.
